Actual Article Body:
Mark A. Garcia

Exploring astronaut health and photographing the Moon and Earth topped the research schedule for the Expedition 75 crew aboard the International Space Station on Tuesday. The orbital residents also kept up life support maintenance following the departure of cargo spacecraft the day before.

Station commander Jessica Meir of NASA assisted flight engineer Sophie Adenot of ESA (European Space Agency) in the Columbus laboratory module during the PhysioTool experiment that monitors an astronaut’s blood flow, mental condition, and sleep quality. Adenot first measured her blood pressure then completed cognitive tasks on a computer to understand how living in microgravity affects her mental capabilities and behavioral style.
